See our privacy policy . Common retaining wall questions in Newcastle What should I look for in a retaining wall quote? A clear retaining wall quote should spell out excavation, materials, drainage, backfill, engineering (if required) and any disposal of old structures. In Newcastle, it is common to see per-metre or per-square-metre rates, but the inclusions matter as much as the headline price. You should also check access assumptions, any allowances for rock or difficult soil, and who is responsible for council approvals. Comparing like-for-like quotes from several contractors helps avoid surprises. What's the cheapest type of retaining wall for a backyard? For many Newcastle homeowners, treated pine or basic timber sleeper walls are among the cheapest options for retaining small to moderate height garden areas. Simple boulder or gabion walls can also be cost-effective in some situations, particularly where rock is readily available. Concrete sleepers and masonry blocks cost more upfront but often last longer and need less maintenance. The cheapest option still has to suit the slope, soil and drainage on your block. What's the difference between a garden edging wall and a structural retaining wall? Garden edging walls are generally low, mainly decorative and only retain small amounts of soil, so they do not usually need engineering or formal approval. Structural retaining walls hold back significant soil loads, often at heights above 600 mm, and they require proper design, footings and drainage. Costs, council requirements and safety considerations are much higher for structural walls. Knowing which category your project falls into helps you budget and plan correctly. What retaining wall materials last the longest? Concrete sleepers, reinforced concrete and quality stone such as sandstone generally provide some of the longest lifespans for retaining walls in NSW conditions.
